title: Government Strategy for Growing Economy and Good Jobs without Over-reliance on Foreign Manpower
what_it_is: Government Strategy for Growing Economy and Good Jobs without Over-reliance on Foreign Manpower

sections.label: Economic strategies and quality jobs
sections.summary: Economic strategies aim to improve Singaporeans' quality of life, and quality jobs come from local and foreign investments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our economic strategies are developed to improve the quality of life and livelihoods for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Quality jobs come from quality investments, both local and foreign.

sections.label: Talent in new growth sectors
sections.summary: Talent is a critical success factor for ICT, Finance and Advanced Manufacturing, which compete on ideas, knowledge and skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Talent is an even more critical success factor for our new growth sectors, such as information and communications technology (ICT), Finance and Advanced Manufacturing, which compete on the basis of ideas, knowledge and skills, more than just size.

sections.label: Foreign complement for competitiveness
sections.summary: Without a local foreign complement in quantity and quality, future generations may lose competitiveness and seek jobs elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It also means the loss of competitiveness and good job opportunities for future generations, where we run the risk that our children and grandchildren will end up having to seek better job opportunities elsewhere because these high and higher paying jobs are no longer available in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Hence, to allow our people and enterprises to punch above our weight, we need a certain local foreign complement, both in terms of quantity and quality.

sections.label: Foreign manpower complements local workforce
sections.summary: Bringing in foreign manpower to complement local workers grows the economy and lets people take higher wage jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we bring in some foreign manpower to complement our local workforce, we can grow the overall size of the economy and, more importantly, allow our people to take on higher wage jobs that are commensurate with their education and aspirations.

sections.label: Win investment, upgrade worker skills
sections.summary: The strategy is to win investment first and quickly upgrade workers' skills for higher paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our strategy is to win the investment first and work hard to quickly upgrade the skills of our workers to take on those higher paying jobs as soon as possible.

sections.label: Growing economy and better jobs
sections.summary: This process grew the economy and created better, higher paying jobs for Singaporeans with an appropriately sized foreign complement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In this process, we have grown the size of the economy, created better job opportunities for Singaporeans, higher paying jobs for Singaporeans, with a foreign complement appropriately sized.

sections.label: Foreign workers and local workforce
sections.summary: The passage states that too many foreign workers, not only lower-skilled ones, make the local workforce feel overwhelmed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Too many foreign workers – and not necessarily just the lower-skilled ones – our local workforce feels overwhelmed.

sections.label: Fair treatment of Singaporeans
sections.summary: It states the Fair Consideration Framework was tightened, errant companies face enforcement and penalties, and Singaporean workers' skills and productivity are improved through education and SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will also ensure that Singaporeans are fairly treated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have the Fair Consideration Framework, which we tightened recently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will not hesitate to act against companies that discriminate against Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To keep it to a manageable level, we must, first, continuously improve the skills and productivity of our Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We are doing this through our education system and continuing lifelong training system, such as SkillsFuture programmes, and we will continue to invest heavily in this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Third, we must ensure that Singaporeans are fairly treated at work and errant companies which treat their Singaporean workers unfairly can expect to face enforcement action and penalties.

sections.label: Example of Singaporean worker
sections.summary: The passage proposes following on from an example used at the last Parliament Sitting of a Singaporean in a job paying $5,000 now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Maybe the best way for me to do is to follow on from the example that I used at the last Parliament Sitting, where I said that: supposing we have a Singaporean working in a job that pays $5,000 now.

sections.label: Local labour force peaking
sections.summary: It states the local labour force will peak over the next 10 years because of the Total Fertility Rate, and with no foreign labour growth the total labour force will peak and decline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Over the next 10 years, our local labour force will peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Labour force participation, even with the extension of the retirement age, the local labour force will peak because of our Total Fertility Rate (TFR).

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: When the local labour force peaks and foreign labour force does not grow, it means that the total labour force will peak and then decline.

sections.label: Changing workforce ratio
sections.summary: It states that if the total is stable while the local workforce peaks and falls, the foreign workforce must take up the slack, so the ratio must change, depending on society's acceptance and varying by sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we maintain a stable total, as local workforce peaks and falls, foreign workforce must take up the slack, which means that the ratio must change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But whether the ratio can change will depend on whether our society can accept the change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is not a straightforward issue and different sectors will have different ratios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is how we must navigate this carefully in the next 10 years to make sure that we take care of the prospects for fellow Singaporeans and, at the same time, make sure that our enterprises have the opportunities to generate new capacity to compete with the world.

sections.label: Question on resident workforce growth
sections.summary: It states the House must ponder what happens if 1% resident workforce growth is not achieved, and that this growth is very significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The question that all of us in this House have to ponder very seriously for the future of our country is this: what if we do not achieve 1% resident workforce growth?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And 1% resident workforce growth is very significant.

sections.label: Next decade numbers
sections.summary: The Member's question on the next decade is being seriously looked at in terms of numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Member's question on the next decade, we are seriously looking at the numbers.

sections.label: Shared understanding of challenges
sections.summary: These issues will be discussed in depth with Members so leaders can share understanding and carry the ground for difficult decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: All these issues, we will be happy to discuss more in depth with Members because I think as leaders in our various capacities, we need to understand and have a shared understanding of these challenges so that we can collectively carry the ground for the difficult decisions that we all have to take together for the next decade.
